rationale: An a-fortiori clause ("much less") moves from a minor case — excellent speech ill-fitting a fool — to a major one — lying lips still less fitting a prince — within one argument, the same shift marked by אַ֝֗ף כִּֽי (oshb:Prov.17.7).
rejected_alternative: No catchword links this verse to 17:6 or 17:8.
device_notes: One escalating argument, not two independent claims.

rationale: A foolish son is diagnosed as a double grief — bitterness “to his father” and to “her who bore him” (web:Prov.17.25) — the parallel dative phrases closing the verse's own complaint.
rejected_alternative: No further cluster is adopted at this seam (see 17:24's disclosure of the shared token).

rationale: A self-isolating man is diagnosed as pursuing appetite against all sound judgment — one complete character-portrait closed on its own verb יִתְגַּלָּֽע. (oshb:Prov.18.1)
device_notes: Self-isolation diagnosed in one unified clause.

rationale: The pair runs an the exact same construct-noun-of-strength phrase twice for opposite referents: 18:10's מִגְדַּל עֹ֭ז "tower of strength" belongs to Yahweh's name and closes וְנִשְׂגָּֽב "and is set safe," while 18:11's קִרְיַ֣ת עֻזּ֑וֹ "city of his strength" belongs to the rich man's wealth and closes נִ֝שְׂגָּבָ֗ה "exalted" — but only “in his own imagination” (web:Prov.18.11; בְּמַשְׂכִּיתֽוֹ). Both the strength-noun (עז/עזו) and the exalted-noun (נשגב) recur across the seam, an antithetic construction run contrasting a true refuge with an imagined one. (oshb:Prov.18.10; oshb:Prov.18.11)
rejected_alternative: Independence is rejected because the second verse's phrase is built to invert the first's claim word-for-word, not merely echo its topic; reading 18:10 alone would lose the ironic twist that ‘his own imagination’ supplies.
observed_substrate_signals: two shared roots, both recurring bare and suffixed at the same syntactic slot
device_notes: Antithetic construction run; true security (divine name) vs. false security (wealth) built on the same construct pattern.

rationale: A man's stomach is filled by the fruit of his own mouth, his own lips' harvest satisfying him — a self-consuming-speech image closed within the verse.
rejected_alternative: Cluster with 18:21 is rejected: both verses use the root "fruit" (here, at 18:21) but 18:20's fruit belongs to the mouth filling the stomach while 18:21's belongs to the tongue's power over death and life — a thematic doubling rather than a repeated construction.
observed_substrate_signals: 18:20 fruit-form מִפְּרִ֣י (oshb:Prov.18.20); 18:21 fruit-form פִּרְיָֽהּ (oshb:Prov.18.21) — different inflected forms of the same root, a different body-part in 18:20 than in 18:21
device_notes: Self-consuming-speech metaphor (mouth's fruit fills the stomach).

rationale: A tov-opener comparative — better the poor walking in integrity than one perverse in speech who is a fool — closes its own מן-clause. (oshb:Prov.19.1)
rejected_alternative: Clustering with 19:2 is rejected: both verses carry the token, but 19:1's is the comparative topic-marker ("better X than Y") while 19:2's sits inside a "not good" predicate mid-verse — the same word in two different syntactic roles, not a repeated construction.
observed_substrate_signals: tov-opener (16 verses book-wide open with this exact token)
device_notes: Better-than comparative; echoes the same opening formula at 17:1 (non-adjacent, disclosed as texture, not evidence).

rationale: Zeal without knowledge is judged "not good," and hasty feet are said to miss the way — two clauses on impulsive ignorance closed within the verse.
rejected_alternative: Independence from 19:1 is retained because 19:1's tov occupies the verse-initial comparative topic-marker slot, while 19:2's occurrence sits inside a mid-verse not-good predicate — the same token in two different syntactic roles, not a repeated construction (oshb:Prov.19.1; oshb:Prov.19.2).
device_notes: Not-good judgment plus a haste-consequence clause.

rationale: Both verses carry the same friend-root רע in the mercenary-friendship theme: 19:6 closes וְכָל הָ֝רֵ֗עַ לְאִ֣ישׁ מַתָּֽן “everyone is a friend to a man who gives gifts” (web:Prov.19.6), and 19:7 opens its second colon with מְ֭רֵעֵהוּ רָחֲק֣וּ מִמֶּ֑נּוּ “his friends avoid him” (web:Prov.19.7) — the same root turned from the flatterer's calculus (v.6) to the poor man's abandonment by that same class of "friend" (v.7), a deliberate two-verse elaboration of one social observation rather than two unrelated maxims. 19:7 also carries a ketiv/qere pair at its closing word (לא/לוֹ); a paseq mark sits in the same verse. (oshb:Prov.19.6; oshb:Prov.19.7)
rejected_alternative: Reading 19:6 and 19:7 as independent is rejected because 19:7's opening colon ("all the relatives of the poor shun him") completes the a-fortiori logic 19:6 sets up — if everyone chases the gift-giver, how much more do even kin flee the poor; the particle opening 19:7 grammatically depends on the claim just made in 19:6.
observed_substrate_signals: shared root at the same "friend" sense in both cola
device_notes: Two-verse elaboration of mercenary friendship; the weaker of this part's clusters, resting more on discourse-logic (dependency) than on an exact repeated lexeme. The friend-root also recurs at 19:4 (oshb:Prov.19.4), non-adjacent; the pairing's force rests on the a-fortiori dependency between 19:6 and 19:7, not on root-exclusivity.

rationale: The exact same noun אִשָּֽׁה/אִשָּׁ֥ה "wife/woman" runs across both verses' second colon in antithesis: 19:13's מִדְיְנֵ֥י אִשָּֽׁה "a wife's quarrels" closes the verse's second colon (colon-final, verse-final), alongside "a foolish son" in the first colon; 19:14's אִשָּׁ֥ה מַשְׂכָּֽלֶת "a prudent wife" instead sits colon-medial in the second colon, occupying the predicate-complement slot immediately after the fronted "from Yahweh" phrase and before the closing "prudent" adjective, alongside "house and riches" as merely human inheritance in the first colon. Both verses pair a father/inheritance first colon with a wife-named second colon, the same two-part frame run twice with opposite content. (oshb:Prov.19.13; oshb:Prov.19.14)
rejected_alternative: Treating the verses as unrelated maxims is rejected because the deliberate repetition of the same wife-noun — verse-final in 19:13, colon-medial in 19:14 — sets up a contrast (quarrelsome wife/dripping vs. prudent wife/Yahweh's gift) that only works read as a pair; taken alone, 19:14's implicit contrast with the preceding verse's wife-image is not recoverable.
observed_substrate_signals: exact repeated noun at the same line-final slot
matching bicolon frame (inheritance colon + wife colon)
device_notes: Antithetic wife-pairing across the seam (quarrelsome vs. prudent, human inheritance vs. Yahweh's gift).

rationale: Slothfulness is said to cast a man into deep sleep, and the idle soul will hunger — two consequence-clauses on laziness closed within the verse.
rejected_alternative: Cluster with 19:16 is rejected: both verses carry the token — 19:15's וְנֶ֖פֶשׁ (oshb:Prov.19.15) is the hungering subject of laziness, while 19:16's נַפְשׁ֑וֹ (oshb:Prov.19.16) is the object kept safe by obedience — the same noun in two different roles, not a repeated construction.
observed_substrate_signals: token shared with 19:16 (disclosed, different grammatical role)

rationale: A man's desirable quality is named as his kindness, and a poor man is set above a liar — two evaluative clauses closed within the verse.
rejected_alternative: No shared token with 19:21 or 19:23; 19:22's second colon opens with the bigram וְטֽוֹב רָ֝שׁ (oshb:Prov.19.22), matching 19:1's opening bigram טֽוֹב רָ֭שׁ (oshb:Prov.19.1) — the two verses sit 21 verses apart (19:1 and 19:22) with no adjacent construction, so this remains disclosed as texture only, not a cluster candidate.
device_notes: Value-judgment couplet, non-adjacent echo of 19:1 disclosed as texture.

rationale: A corrupt witness is said to mock justice, and the mouth of the wicked gulps down iniquity — two clauses on courtroom corruption closed within the verse.
rejected_alternative: Cluster with 19:29 is rejected: both verses carry the root — 19:28's מִשְׁפָּ֑ט (oshb:Prov.19.28) names the legal process being mocked, while 19:29's שְׁפָטִ֑ים (oshb:Prov.19.29) names the punishments prepared for scoffers — the same root in two distinct senses (process vs. penalty), a homograph-adjacent split rather than a repeated construction.
